title: What Does One More AI Agent Contribute? A Microeconomic Review of Delegation, Search, and Verification
abstract: What does a project gain from one more AI agent? This selective narrative review connects the microeconomics of delegation, innovation contests, public goods, information, and market design to recent cases in mathematics, physics, biomedical research, software, and exchange. The answer depends on the assignment: it can yield a competing solution, improve a shared input, or check an uncertain first report. The contest literature emphasizes the diversity of attempts, the economics of cumulative innovation emphasizes downstream reuse, and information economics asks what a second report reveals conditional on the first. Which return a project can capture also depends on who supplies review and what the acceptance rule measures. Comparing a public proof desk with evidence extraction for rare diseases illustrates why duplicate work can waste resources in one assignment and be the purpose of another. We propose ways to distinguish these mechanisms using assignment, audit, and reuse records.
